subject: EU pilot retention & erase evidence — requested clarifications
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@finledger.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinLedger Security <security@finledger.com>
Date: 2026-05-14T09:18:00Z
Subject: EU pilot retention & erase evidence — quick clarifications

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. A couple of follow-ups for our compliance team so we can finalize the pilot SOW:  
1) For the hosted Redwood API in our EU pilot region — by default, which of the following are stored and for how long: raw request text (prompts), intermediate/streamed token fragments, final model output, and server-side telemetry (latency/errors)?
2) If we (FinLedger) request an immediate erasure for a set of sessions, what is the expected timeline for the data to be unrecoverable from all storage tiers? We need this to align with our internal 72-hour SLA for remediation requests.
3) What form of "proof of deletion" can Redwood provide? Our auditors want a machine-verifiable artifact they can attach to tickets.
4) Are there exceptions where attachments / file blobs uploaded with the prompt are retained longer (e.g., for debug or safety review)?

Can you point us to any sample evidence artifacts?

Appreciate a concise answer we can forward to security.

— Marta
Marta Lopez
Head of Privacy, FinLedger

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@finledger.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-14T13:04:00Z
Subject: Re: EU pilot retention & erase evidence — quick clarifications

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up top, then details below:  
- Stored by default (hosted EU region): prompts and final outputs are retained for 60 days; streamed fragments are transient and not persisted beyond the session unless the session is explicitly finalized; telemetry (latency/errors/trace ids) retained for 365 days for operational/SLAs.
- Erasure SLA (typical): background deletion starts immediately and standard timeline for full eradication from hot + warm tiers is ~48 hours; deep archival purges (if the data hit longer-term snapshot storage) can take up to 7 days. We can commit to a 72-hour window for the pilot and document it in the SOW.
- Proof of deletion: we can provide a signed deletion token (SHA256 digest) plus an audit record showing job id(s), timestamps, and the storage shards cleaned. Sample is attached (erasure-proof-sample.pdf).
- Attachments: file blobs uploaded as part of a request are treated as artifacts and by default follow the same 60-day retention; safety/debugging flags can cause temporary retention beyond that window (only with customer's explicit consent).

I'll let Karthik add the low-level details on streamed fragments and how we mark items transient vs persisted.

Best,
Olga
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@finledger.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-15T08:30:00Z
Subject: Re: EU pilot retention & erase evidence — quick clarifications

Hi Marta — a few technical clarifications to back up Olga's summary:  
- Streamed token fragments: our serving runtime buffers fragments in-memory and in ephemeral GPUs for the duration of the session. We do not materialize those fragments to persistent blob storage unless the session is explicitly flushed (finalized) or a customer enables session rehydration. For the EU pilot the default is "no flush" unless you call the finalize endpoint.
- Finalization semantics: when a session is finalized we write a canonical request/response pair to the request-store and index it for search & metrics. Those canonical records constitute the "stored prompts + outputs" counted against the 60-day TTL.
- Telemetry separation: operational telemetry and audit logs are sharded to a separate retention tier and encrypted with customer-provided KMS for Private deployments; for hosted EU tenants we keep telemetry for 365 days to satisfy SLA investigations. We can provide filtered telemetry extracts for audits on request.
- Erasure pipeline: erase requests create a reproducible job that: 1) marks records as deleted in the index; 2) enqueues physical object deletion across object-store tiers; 3) runs a final consistency scan and emits a signed deletion token stamped with the job id. The signed token plus the job log is what we include in the erasure-proof artifact.
- Snapshots & backups: we do not include ephemeral session buffers in backups. If data reached snapshot/backup tier, the job coordinates with snapshot lifecycle to mark and purge the relevant snapshot segment — this is the stage that can extend to a few days.

I'll attach a short diagram (redwood-data-flow.png) that maps where each artifact lands. Happy to walk your security team through the erasure token structure tomorrow.

— Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
